Show enough of his canonical head and blue-coated arm, both distinct optical endpoints and their connection to verify direction. Keep perspective mild: do not use an extreme frontal lens close-up that conceals which end is which. A giant circular lens facing the viewer is NOT the requested composition.

Use character_sheet for the exact captain face, eye patch, beard, hat and blue cuff, and entry_identity for the correctly oriented telescope. The small end belongs at the visible eye, never the patched eye or an unsupported hand gesture. Show a plausible barrel-supporting grip. Do not mirror the character, swap telescope ends, point the objective back toward his face, or put an eyeball/face inside the tube. This ownership and agency cue is actual optical use, not an anonymous cuff beside a lens.

The topic-relevant subject lies beyond the outward-pointing objective; the target-world reference supplies only that subject's medium, texture, palette and initial clue. Do not paint a mini-world over the captain's face or onto the eyecup. The camera will match into his outward-looking optical point of view in B, not physically fly backward from the objective into his face. Keep the scene edge-to-edge without a page/card border, circular vignette, grid, embedded text or extra limbs. The eventual last frame contains neither host nor spyglass.

EPISODE TOPIC: Could You Live Forever on a Desert Island??
EPISODE DIRECTION: Full-bleed 9:16 tropical food shelter, oblique rear-three-quarter view of the seasoned blue-coated captain pausing skeptically beside abundant drying fish, coconuts, and a full water barrel while a plate repeats only fish and coconut. His visible unpatched eye meets the spyglass’s small rear eyepiece; one hand holds it firmly while the other supports the brown-and-brass barrel extending outward to the clearly larger objective aimed at the food. Mild perspective, bright shaded island light, readable abundance-versus-variety tension, no text or vignette.
